# Source-only review of f368d4ff11

The commit supplies a concrete Δ₁ native Foundation theory and a one-way external model bridge. These are useful prerequisites for the reverse ZF-to-validator comparison; they do not finish the proposed R1/R2/R3 chain or the PA machine endpoint. No mathematical source blocker was found. This is source review, not a fresh elaboration or axiom-audit result.

Provenance: f368d4ff1129debb624d7ff01b9d8b5f2ffb6b4c, merged as 4e560f8a6428935896c6db1bf43c90ead57a6ec5. Author Vladimir Reshetnikov, coauthor Claude Opus 5.5. All five changed files currently equal their committed bytes. The accompanying JSON pins those files and supporting interfaces. No selected BusyBeaver source was changed by this commit.

## Exact theorem scope

`NativeGicDelta1.lean:44` defines the ordinary GIC skeleton. The support clause permits arbitrary x; the coverage clause bounds x by a. Its de Bruijn substitutions preserve the intended argument order, and universal closure captures the remaining free parameters. Lines56,130,139 give typed and raw internal bodies and their equality in every arithmetic model of IΣ₁. The fixed Σ₁ graph begins at212; `GicR.defined` at257 proves Δ₁ recognition in every such model.

`gicTheory_delta1` at274 proves standard schema membership using the generic Nat quote recognizer, and properness in arbitrary IΣ₁ models. The raw identity and lower-bound lemmas at175 and197 concern standard Nat quotes specifically. This is sufficient for the stated Δ₁ instance; it is not yet an axiom-introduction theorem for every arbitrary internal core.

`NativeTheory.lean:53,55` defines `EQ ∪ {containerAx, irAx} ∪ gicTheory` and its Δ₁ instance. `collection` at93 covers every ordinary native matrix and environment. `models_cpgic` at114 gives native CP/GIC and raw irreflexivity from an external Foundation model of this theory. The semantic section assumes a nonempty set structure modeling nativeTheory, not an arbitrary arithmetic model hosting internal proofs. The equality-free premise in the CP/GIC target is safely unused because collection already covers all ordinary matrices.

## R1/R2/R3 relevance

The maintained proposal in `pa_internalization.md:742–765` asks for three distinct pieces. This commit implements R1's concrete theory/recognizer construction. It does not supply R1's additionally requested standard-proof equivalence with `BProv NativeAx`. Its external model bridge is useful for R3's fixed-sentence obligations but is not a represented WF interpretation. Neither R2's arbitrary-internal Foundation-to-C254 translation nor R3's `Provable ZF ⊥ → Provable nativeTheory ⊥` in every IΣ₁ model appears here. The scheduler/control/binary PA comparison remains separate.

The proposal's introductory “nothing below is implemented yet” at733 is stale for the theory-construction portion. A narrow frontier update should mark that portion supplied while retaining the standard-proof sanity check and R2/R3 obligations. The module header and README's “R1” label should be read at this restricted construction scope.

## Useful next lemma

`ModelCodedSchemaAxioms.schemaRecognizer_of_closed_body` at25 and the internal binary-core identity pattern at50 give a direct next source task: GIC axiom membership for an arbitrary shift-fixed internal binary core. Derive its identity substitution from `val_gicSubst01Const`, combine `subst01_le_gicBodyVal` with `gicBodyVal_eq`, prove body shift-fixedness, and introduce recognizer/union membership. This is a proposed extension, not a defect in the existing Δ₁ instance. Arbitrary free-parameter closure and internal derivation translation remain additional work; standard-quote correctness alone does not discharge them.

## Review scope

Read all284 lines of NativeGicDelta1,121 lines of NativeTheory and11 lines of NativeTheoryAudit, plus relevant recognizer, translation, CP/GIC, native-theory and model-coded-schema interfaces. The audit has five named `#print axioms` probes and zero typed clients. The commit message reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, but no actual terminal evidence was audited here. No compiler, checker, version query, simulator or build was invoked; no maintained file was edited. A reviewer-only metadata attempt used the wrong BusyBeaver dependency path and failed before writing the review; correcting that path did not affect any source.
